1.8.3.1.1. Add an instance in Service Manager
Integration Suite (SMIS)

Applies to User roles: System Administrator

To set up the integration from Service Manager to RTSM, you must add an instance of this
integration in the Service Manager Integration Suite (SMIS). Note that additional setup is
required on the APM OMi side for integration from APM to Service Manager. For details, refer
to the Business Service Management Operations Manager i Extensibility Guide.

To add the SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance:

   1. Click Tailoring > Integration Manager. Integration Instance Manager opens.

   2. Click Add. The Integration Template Selection wizard opens.

   3. Select SMBSM_DOWNTIME from the Integration Template list. Ignore the Import
     Mapping checkbox, which has no effect on this integration.

   4. Click Next. The Integration Instance Information page opens.

   5. Do the following:

          • Modify the Name and Version fields to the exact values you need.

          • In the Interval Time(s) field, enter a value based on your business needs in regard
          to downtime exchange frequency. Note that a short interval time can be safe because
          the next scheduled task will not start until the previous task is completed and the
          interval time passed.

          • In the Max Retry Times field, enter a value. This is the maximum allowed number of
          retries (for example, 10) for each failed task.

          • In the Log File Directory field, specify a directory where log files of the integration
          will be stored. This must be a directory that already exists on the Service Manager
          server. By default, logging message is output to sm.log .

          • (Optional) In the SM Server field, specify a display name for the Service Manager
          server host. For example, my_local_SM.

          • (Optional) In the Endpoint Server field, specify a display name for the APM server
          host. For example, my_APM_1.

          • (Optional) In the Log Level field, change the log level from INFO (default) to another
          level. For example, WARNING.

          • (Optional) If you want this integration instance to be automatically enabled when
          the Service Manager Server service is started, select Run at system startup.

   6. Click Next. The Integration Instance Parameters page opens.

1.8.3.1.2. Tailor Service Manager to handle
phase change

Applies to User roles: System Administrator, Implementer

In the Service Manager Change Management module, authorized users can manually change
the phase of a change record. If the phase is changed to the one prior to the final approval
phase in the SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance, the system will check if there are existing planned
downtimes that have been set to Ready. If such downtimes exist, a window will open and
provide two options for the corresponding planned downtimes:

     Click Yes to withdraw the corresponding planned downtimes from UCMDB. The changes
     or tasks need to be approved again to synchronize with UCMDB at another time.
     Click No. There will be no change to the planned downtimes even if the actual status of
     the changes or tasks aren't approved.

            Note

           Note: To disable the pop-up window when withdrawing the planned downtimes,
           you need to set the WithdrawDowntime parameter to false in the
           SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance. This operation may cause some unapproved
           planned downtimes to be synchronized to APM.

With Process Designer (PD) Content Pack 2 applied in Service Manager, you can tailor the
process to transit changes or tasks from one phase that's after the final approval phase in the
SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance to another that's prior to the final approval phase.To withdraw
the related planned downtime for this kind of transition, you need to add a rule set for the
transition in the Closed Loop Incident Process (CLIP) solution. Refer to the following steps:

   1. Go to the target workflow that needs tailoring.
   2. Select the transition that moves a phase from before the final approval phase to after the

     final approval phase.
   3. In the Rule Sets section, click Add and select the clip.downtime.withdraw rule set.
   4. Click OK to save the workflow.

1.8.3.1.3. Set up integration in APM

If you have Universal CMDB (UCMDB) between Service Manager and APM, you can use
UCMDB to maintain downtime CIs that are populated from Service Manager, and APM will
consume them through UCMDB. There is no need to set up an integration in APM (RTSM).

If you don't have UCMDB between Service Manager and APM, you need to set up a new
integration in APM (RTSM) to proactively pull the scheduled downtime from Service Manager.

Being an instance of UCMDB, RTSM embeds in APM and performs the expected functions of a
CMDB. RTSM reconciles and stores configuration items (CIs) that represent the IT environment
components and helps organizations understand the relationships between these components
and track their configuration.

Make sure you have applied the latest content package and update to RTSM. For instructions
on how to set up a downtime integration in RTSM, refer to the Data Flow Management Guide.

1.8.3.1.4. Set up integration in Universal CMDB

This task sets up a new integration in Universal CMDB (UCMDB) to proactively pull the
scheduled downtime from Service Manager. Make sure you have applied the latest Content
Package and update to your UCMDB.

To set up the Universal CMDB adapter:

   1. Sign in to your UCMDB system as an administrator.
   2. Create an integration point that connects to your Service Manager server. For example,

     SM980. Make sure this integration point uses the latest ServiceManager Adapter 9-x.
   3. Click Managers > Data Flow Management > Integration Studio. UCMDB displays a list of

     integration points.
   4. Select sm931 in the Integration Point list. Make sure the SM Configuration Items

     Population job and the SM Relations Population job run first.

   5. Create two integration jobs in the integration point.

        1. Create a new job including the CLIP Down Time Population job definition. Under
           Scheduler Definition, select the Scheduler enabled checkbox and set the Repeat
           Interval to 1 Minute. Click OK to save the job.

        2. Create another new job including the CI To Down Time CI With Connection job
           definition. Under Scheduler Definition, select the Scheduler enabled checkbox and
           set the Repeat Interval to 1 Minute. Click OK to save the job.

     Pay attention to the running order and run the CLIP Down Time Population job first. You
     can set the two jobs as schedule-based and set the schedule interval according to your
     needs.

   6. After the two jobs have finished successfully, go back to the Modeling section and check
     the CIs with the type ScheduledDowntime. Make sure their relationships are created.

            Note

           Note: If no related CIs exist in UCMDB when creating relationships, the population
           will fail or succeed with a warning. To disable the warning, remove the downtime CI
           that doesn't have related CIs in UCMDB.

1.9. Operations Bridge Manager (OBM)

Note: Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) was known as OMi before version 2018.05.
There are two variations of integrating Service Manager (SM) with OBM. One case uses the
RTSM contained in OBM as the CMDB, and needs only one data flow probe (DFP1), which is
installed in the OBM deployment. The other case uses a UCMDB, and needs two data flow
probes (DFP1 installed on the UCMDB server and DFP2 in the OBM deployment).

Point-to-point integration

OBM is integrated with Service Manager directly, using OBM's Run Time Service Model
(RTSM) as CMDB, as shown in the following figure.

We recommend installing the Data Flow Probe 1 (DFP1) in the OBM deployment.

Integration using a Universal Configuration Management
Database (UCMDB)

OBM is set up using an external UCMDB, as shown in the following figure.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1549 of 1727
                                        Service Manager 9.81

We recommend installing the Data Flow Probe 1 (DFP1) on the UCMDB server and the Data
Flow Probe 2 (DFP2) in the OBM deployment.

Data flow probes

Two different data flow probes need to be installed. They have different purposes.

     DFP1 is needed for the following:

           Populating the RTSM with CIs (Data Population)
           Federation

           Topology synchronization (CIs) between RTSM and SM in the case of a point-to-
           point integration

           OR

           Topology synchronization (CIs) between UCMDB and OBM and between UCMDB
           and SM in case of using an external UCMDB

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1550 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

     DFP2 is needed for federation only.

Prerequisites

If you are using a standalone CMDB, you need to do the following before continuing with the
OBM-SM integration:

     Set up the integration between OBM and UCMDB.
     Integrate UCMDB with SM to synchronize CIs from UCMDB to SM.

For details, see Universal CMDB.

Integration options

     Incident exchange between SM and OBM. OBM enables you to forward events from
     OBM to SM. Forwarded events and subsequent event changes are synchronized back
     from SM to OBM. You can also drill down from OBM events to SM incidents. For details,
     see Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration.

     Downtime exchange between OBM and SM. OBM enables you to forward downtimes
     (also known as outages) from OBM to SM, and from SM to OBM. The downtime defined in
     OBM is directed to SM as an incident, and vice versa. For details, see Downtime
     Exchange between OBM and Service Manager.

     View planned changes and incident details in Service Health. This integration enables
     you to view planned changes and incident details in the Changes and Incidents tab on the
     360° View page in Service Health. For details, see OBM - Service Manager integration
     overview.

     The Business Impact Report integration is part of the Closed Loop Incident Process
     (CLIP) solution. When deployed as part of the OBM solution, Incident Management users
     can launch an impact report from an incident in context with the incident's affected CI.
     Service desk agents can validate the updated status of the business impact to categorize
     and prioritize the incident accordingly.

     For details, see the CLIP page in the APM Business Impact Report (BIR).

1.9.1. Incident Exchange (OBM - SM)
integration

The Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration is a bidirectional integration between incident
records in Service Manager and events in Operations Bridge Manager (OBM).

This integration requires configurations on both product sides. For details, see Incident
Exchange (OBM - SM) integration setup.

            Note

           Service Manager can integrate with multiple OBM servers. For details, see Add an
           integration instance for each OBM server.

Service Manager can accept requests that based on RESTful from OBM to create Incidents in
Service Manager, based on events information in OBM. When Service Manager accepts an
incident creation request from a remote OBM server, it creates an incident record and
automatically assigns it to an existing group based on certain field values. Incident
Management users can view the details of the related OBM event by clicking the View OBM
Event menu option from the incident record. See Drill down to the OBM event details from an
incident.

When an Incident Management user makes any changes to the incident record, Service
Manager sends an update request to the OBM RESTful web service interface. Hence, it
automatically synchronizes the changes to the corresponding event in OBM. In the event of a
synchronization failure, a queuing mechanism will synchronize the changes again. See
Synchronization of incident changes back to Operations Bridge Manager (OBM).

System administrators can configure global settings to decide whether and when incident
records opened from OBM events can be automatically closed. However, Incident Management
users can mark individual OBM incident records as eligible or ineligible for automatic closure.
See Configure automatic closure for OBM incidents and Mark an incident for automatic closure.

1.9.1.1. Incident Exchange (OBM - SM)
integration setup

The Incident Exchange (OBM-SM) integration requires you to complete the following
configuration tasks on the Service Manager and Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) systems.

            Note

           Configuring Service Manager web service integrations in a network environment
           using a firewall or proxy server requires additional configuration. For details, see
           Web Services with a proxy server.

   1. Create user accounts for the Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration.

     This task creates a user account on each product side for the two systems to connect to
     each other and synchronize data.

   2. Configure an event forwarding rule in OBM.

     This task configures a rule for the OBM server to forward events to the Service Manager
     server.

   3. Configure the Service Manager server as a connected server in OBM.
     This task configures the connection settings for the target Service Manager server. If you
     need to integrate Service Manager with more than one OBM server, perform this task on
     each of the OBM servers.

   4. (Optional) Add custom attributes and map to SM fields.

     This task adds your own custom attributes in the Groovy script selected for the SM server
     and maps the attributes to appropriate fields in SM.

   5. Enable event drill-down from Service Manager into OBM

     This task sets up Service Manager operators as valid users with appropriate permissions
     in OBM. These permissions are required for the users to perform event drill-down from
     Service Manager to OBM.
   6. Enable incident drill-down from the OBM Event Browser.

     This task configures the Service Manager web tier in the sm:ServiceManagerAdapter
     script in OBM.

   7. (Optional)Configure SSL for the Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration .

     This task is needed if your OBM server requires HTTPS connections. If SSL is not
     configured in this case, changes on incidents that are created from OBM will not be able
     to be synchronized back to OBM.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1554 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

   8. Configure the Instance Count in the SMOBM integration template.

     This task is needed only when you use more than one OBM server. The Instance Count
     setting defines the allowed number of SM-OBM integration instances in Service Manager
     (default: 1).

   9. Add an integration instance for each OBM server.

     This task creates and enables an instance of this integration in Integration Manager
     (SMIS). A separate integration instance is required for each OBM server.

 10. (Optional) Enable LW-SSO for the Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration.

     Lightweight Single Sign-On (LW-SSO) is optional but recommended for the Incident
     Exchange (OBM - SM) integration. This task includes enabling LW-SSO in the Service
     Manager server and Web tier, as well as in OBM.

 11. (Optional) Configure automatic closure for OBM incidents.

     By default, automatic closure is disabled for OBM incidents. System administrators can
     enable automatic closure and further configure under what conditions OBM incidents can
     be automatically closed.

 12. (Optional) Change the default assignment group for OBM incidents.

     When created, OBM incidents are automatically assigned with an assignment group
     based on their certain field values and a predefined default assignment group. System
     Administrators can change the default assignment group setting ( Application).

 13. Test the connection

     This task sends an event to the OBM server that matches the filter you defined (in our
     example filter, the severity value is Critical), and then verifies that the event is forwarded
     to Service Manager as expected.

 14. (Optional) Synchronize attributes

     Not all attributes are synchronized back from SM to OBM by default. This task changes
     the out-of-box behavior regarding which attributes are synchronized upon change.

1.9.1.1.1. Create user accounts for the Incident
Exchange (OBM-SM) integration

Applies to User roles: System Administrator

The Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration is bidirectional. Synchronizing events and
incidents between the Service Manager and OBM systems requires you to set up integration
accounts for the two systems to access each other.

   1. Create an operator record with system administration privileges in Service Manager. For
     details, see Creating operator records.

     This is the user account that the OBM server uses to access Service Manager and to
     forward events to Service Manager.

     Later, when configuring the Service Manager server as a connected server in OBM, you
     need to specify this operator's login name and password on the Outgoing Connection
     tab. See Configure the Service Manager server as a connected server in OBM.

   2. Create a user account with system administration privileges on each OBM server. For
     details, see the OBM online help.

     This is the user account that Service Manager uses to access the OBM server and to
     synchronize incident changes back.

     Later, when configuring the Service Manager server as a connected server in OBM, you
     must specify this user's login name as the Name of the Service Manager server on the
     General tab. Next, specify this user's password as the Password on the IncOBMng
     Connection tab. See Configure the Service Manager server as a connected server in
     OBM.

     Also, you need to specify the same user account when adding an SM - OBM integration
     instance for each OBM server (the username and Password parameters). See Add an
     integration instance for each OBM server.

1.9.1.1.2. Configure the Service Manager
server as a connected server in OBM

To synchronize changes between OBM events and Service Manager incidents, you need to
configure a connected server within OBM to correctly identify the target Service Manager
server instance.
To configure the Service Manager server as a target connected server, perform the following
steps:

   1. Log on to OBM as a system administrator.

   2. Navigate to the Connected Servers user interface:

     Administration > Setup and Maintenance > Connected Servers

   3. Click the New button, and then select External Event Processing to open the Create New
     Server Connection dialog box.

   4. In the Display Name field, enter a descriptive name for the Service Manager server.
     In the Name field, enter the user name of the OBM user account you created for Service
     Manager to access the OBM server. See Create user accounts for the Incident Exchange
     (OBM - SM) integration.

     Make a note of the Name of the new target server. You need to provide it later on as the
     username when configuring the Service Manager server to communicate with the OBM
     server. See Add an integration instance for each OBM server.

     Optionally, enter a description for the new target server.

     Make sure that the Active checkbox is selected.

     Click Next.
   5. In the Server Properties pane, enter the following information:

     Fully Qualified DNS Name: The fully qualified domain name of the target Service
     Manager server.

     CI Type: Select Service Manager System from the list.

     Keep the Advanced Delivery Options as default.

     Click Next.
   6. In the Integration Type dialog box, you can choose between using a Groovy script

     adapter, or the Event Synchronization Web Service.

        1. As a Service Manager Groovy script adapter is provided for integrating with Service
           Manager, select Call Script Adapter.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1557 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                         Service Manager 9.81

     2. In the Script Name field, select sm:ServiceManagerAdapter.

     3. Click Next.

7. In the Outgoing Connection dialog, enter the credentials (user name, password, and port
  number) to connect to the Service Manager server and to forward events to that server.

     1. In the User Name and Password fields, enter the Service Manager user credentials
        you created for the integration. See Create user accounts for the Incident Exchange
        (OBM - SM) integration.

     2. Repeat the password entry in the Verify Password field.

     3. In the Port field, enter the communications port of the Service Manager server.

        The Service Manager server configuration file (sm.ini) defines the http and http
        ports. Enter the http port when Service Manager is running in http mode, or enter
        the https port when it is running in secure http mode.

                      Tip

                   If you click Set default port, the Port field is automatically populated
                   with the default port (13080 for http or 13443 for secure http). However,
                   your actual Service Manager ports may differ from the default values.

     4. If the Service Manager server uses secure http (SSL) mode, select the Use Secure
        HTTP checkbox. If it uses http mode, make sure the checkbox is not checked.

     5. If the Use Secure HTTP checkbox is selected, download and install a copy of the
        Service Manager server’s SSL certificate by clicking the link Retrieve from Server,
        or Import from File if the certificate is available in a local file.

     6. Make sure that the Enable Synchronize and Transfer Control checkbox is checked.

        When the Enable Synchronize and Transfer Control flag is set, an Operations
        Management operator is then able to transfer ownership of the event to the target
        connected server. If the flag is not set, then the option Synchronize and Transfer
        Control doesn't appear in the list of forwarding types when configuring forwarding
        rules.

        Also, note that if the Enable Synchronize and Transfer Control flag is not set for any
        target connected server, the Transfer Control to option doesn't appear at all in the
        Event Browser context menu.

        If a specific server is configured without the Enable Synchronize and Transfer
        Control flag set, then that server is unavailable in the Event Browser context menu
        as a server to which you can transfer ownership.

     7. Click Test Connection. A Success or ERROR hyperlink appears.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1558 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                         Service Manager 9.81

        If an error appears, click the link to get a more detailed message. Fix the problems
        and try again until the connection is successful.
     8. Click Next.
8. If, in addition to automatically generating Service Manager incidents from OBM events,
  you want to also be able to drill-down into Service Manager, you need to specify the fully
  qualified DNS name and port of the Service Manager web application server (for example,
  Tomcat).

               Note

             To enable incident drill-down to Service Manager, you must have the Service
             Manager web tier deployed on a web application server.

  In the Event Drilldown dialog box, configure the Fully Qualified DNS Name and Port of
  the web application server on which the Service Manager web tier is deployed.

               Note

             If you don't specify a server in the Event Drilldown dialog box, it is assumed
             that the web tier is deployed on the same host as the Service Manager server.

  If the web application server communicates with the browser over SSL (secure HTTP),
  select the Use Secure HTTP checkbox.
  Click Next.
9. The next thing to do is to enable event changes to be synchronized back from Service
  Manager to OBM. For this you need to provide credentials for the Service Manager server
  to access the OBM server in the IncOBMng Connection dialog box.

     1. Select the Accept event changes from external processing server checkbox.

                      Note

                   If Enable Synchronize and Transfer Control was previously selected,
                   the Accept event changes from external processing server option is
                   assumed, and can't be disabled.

     2. Enter the password of the OBM user account that you created for the Service
        Manager server to access the OBM server. See Create user accounts for the
        Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration.

     3. Make sure the User Name (auto-generated) matches the one of the OBM user
        account you created. If not, click the General tab, and change the Name field to the
        correct value.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1559 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

        4. Click Finish. The target Service Manager server now appears in the list of
           Connected Servers.

1.9.1.1.4. Configure an event forwarding rule in
OBM

Suppose you have configured the Service Manager server as a connected server in
Application Performance Management (APM) Operations Bridge Manager (OBM). Next, you
need to configure an event forwarding rule for the OBM server to forward events to Service
Manager.

   1. Sign in to OBM as a system administrator.
   2. Navigate to Administration > Event Processing > Automation > Event Forwarding.
   3. Click the New Item button.
   4. In the Display Name field, enter a name for the rule. For example, smserver1 .
   5. Optionally, enter a description for the rule.
   6. In the Event Filter field, click the Manage Filters button.

     Click New, and then select New Simple Filter or New Advanced Filter.
     Follow the screen prompts to configure the rule. For example, for Severity, select Critical.
     Click OK.
   7. In the Target Servers field, select the Service Manager server you configured as a
     connected server, and then click the Add button.
     The details of the target server are displayed.
   8. Click OK.
     The Event Forwarding Rules list displays the forwarding rule.

1.9.1.1.5. Enable event drill-down from Service
Manager into OBM

An OBM administrator must configure the operators as valid users with appropriate
permissions in OBM. Hence, these operators are able to perform event drill-down from SM into
the OBM user interface using a URL launch of the Event Browser,

            Note

           Without valid user names, or if a user doesn't have the required viewing
           permissions, trying to perform a URL launch of the OBM Event Browser from SM
           results in an empty browser window.

User account requirements

     If you have configured SM to use Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication, set up each user
     in OBM with the same user name that's used by the SM operator to sign in to SM and
     perform the URL call. (The password of each OBM user can be any string, but not empty.)
     After successfully logging on to SM, the OBM users can launch the OBM Event Browser
     without further authentication.

     For details on setting up SSO, see System Administration > Integrations > Service
     Manager integration methods and tools > Integration Manager > Using LW-SSO with
     integrations in the SM online help.

     If SM isn't configured to use SSO authentication, set up each user with the same user
     name that's used by the SM operator and specify a valid password. The users are
     required to enter their user name and password when launching the OBM Event Browser.

Required user permissions

You must grant the permission Events assigned to user including the required actions to each
OBM user.

To do this, follow these steps:

   1. Select Administration > Users > Users, Groups, and Roles.
   2. Select a role or create a new one. In the Permissions section, go to the Operations

     Console category, select Events and specify the actions users can perform on Events
     assigned to user.
   3. You can optionally grant the permission to view events not assigned to each user.

Suppose you have configured the Service Manager server as a connected server in Operations

   1. Configure the Service Manager web tier in the sm:ServiceManagerAdapter script in
     OBM

   2. Set the queryhashcode parameter in the Service Manager server configuration file

Configure the Service Manager web tier in the
sm:ServiceManagerAdapter script in OBM

To do this, follow these steps:
   1. Sign in to OBM as a system administrator.
   2. Navigate to Administration > Setup and Maintenance > Connected Servers.
   3. Click the Manage Scripts icon in the toolbar.
   4. Click the sm:ServiceManagerAdapter script, and then click the Edit icon.
   5. On the Script tab, locate the following string in the script:

          private static final String SM_WEB_TIER_NAME

   6. Change the value of this parameter to the name of your Service Manager web tier. For
     example, if your web tier file name is sm-9.xx.war, change the parameter value to:

          private static final String SM_WEB_TIER_NAME = 'sm-9.xx'

   7. Click OK to save the script.

Set the queryhashcode parameter in the Service Manager
server configuration file

To do this, follow these steps:
   1. Stop the Service Manager server.
   2. Add the following parameter to the server configuration file ( sm.ini ):
      queryhashcode:<host>:<port>
     Where: <host>:<port> must be the same as the Service Manager hostname and port
     number that are configured in the Service Manager web tier configuration file ( web.xml ).

   3. Restart the Service Manager server.

1.9.1.1.7. Configure SSL for the Incident
Exchange (OBM - SM) integration

Applies to User roles: System Administrator

When Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) or Service Manager is configured to accept HTTPS
connections only, you must configure SSL for the integration. If you don't do so, changes on an
incident that's created from OBM can't be synchronized back to OBM.

            Note

           The following steps describe how you do so by using the built-in keytool in Service
           Manager, and the file paths are for Windows only. Be sure to change the file paths
           accordingly if your Service Manager system is running on Linux.

If OBM is configured to accept HTTPS connections only, do the following:

   1. Import the OBM root certificate to the Service Manager server trusted keystore.

     The following is an example of the command line:

      <SM Install path>\server\RUN\jre\bin\keytool -import -alias myCA -file <.pem file of your
     APM root certificate> -keystore <SM Install path>\Server\RUN\jre\lib\security\cacerts -
     storepass <changeit>

     Where: changeit is the default password of the trusted keystore. Change it to your own
     password if you changed it previously.

  2. Add the following parameters to the Service Manager server configuration file (<SM
     install path>\Server\RUN\sm.ini):

      truststoreFile:<SM install path>\Server\RUN\jre\lib\security\cacerts

      truststorePass:<changeit>

   3. Restart the Service Manager Server service.

For bidirectional SSL, you need to enable SSL in Service Manager first, and then import the SM
certs to the OBM trusted keystore. Follow these steps:

   1. Enable SSL on the Service Manager server. For more information, see Secure Sockets
     Layer (SSL) encryption.

   2. Run the following command to export the SM certs.

      <SM Install path>\server\RUN\jre\bin\keytool -export -alias smserver -file sm-
     certificate.crt -keystore <SM Install path>\server\RUN\smserver.p12 -storepass
     <serverkeystore>

   3. Run the following command to import the SM certs to the OBM trusted keystore.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1567 of 1727
                                                                Service Manager 9.81

      opr-cert-mgmt.bat -import smserver sm-certificate.crt

1.9.1.1.8. Configure the Instance Count in the
SMOMi integration template

Applies to User roles: System Administrator
Service Manager can integrate with more than one Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) server.
However, this integration only allows one OBM server by default. If you need to integrate
Service Manager with more than one OBM server, you need to configure the Instance Count
setting in the SMOMi integration template, as described below.

   1. Sign in to Service Manager as a system administrator.

   2. Type db in the command line, and press Enter.

   3. In the Table field, type SMISRegistry , and click Search.
     The SMIS integration template form opens.

   4. Click Search.
     A list of SMIS integration templates opens.

   5. Select SMOMi from the list.

   6. In the Instance Count field, change the value of 1 to the number of OBM servers that you
     want to integrate with Service Manager. For example, if you need two OBM servers,
     change the value to 2.

   7. Click Save.

1.9.1.1.9. Add an integration instance for each
OBM server

Applies to User roles: System Administrator

Once you have completed your configuration in Operations Bridge Manager (OBM), and have
changed the Instance Count setting in the SMOMi integration template (which is needed only
when you have multiple OBM servers), you are ready to add and enable a separate integration
instance in Service Manager for each OBM server. For example, if you have two OBM servers,
you must configure two SMOMi integration instances.

Support of multiple OBM servers

As of version 9.34, Service Manager can integrate with multiple OBM servers. This is
implemented through the Instance Count setting and the omi.mgr.id parameter in the SMOMi
integration template.

By default, the SMOMi integration template supports only one integration instance. If you have
multiple OBM servers, before you proceed, make sure you have already updated the Instance
Count setting in the SMOMi integration template. For details, see Configure the Instance Count
in the SMOMi integration template.

When using the omi.mgr.id parameter, keep the following in mind:

     If you have only one OBM server (and hence need only one SMOMi integration instance),
     you must either correctly configure this parameter or clear the entire row of this
     parameter (both the parameter name and value) in the SMOMi integration instance,
     otherwise the integration will not work.
     If you have multiple OBM servers (and hence need multiple SMOMi integration instances),
     you must correctly configure this parameter in all SMOMi integration instances. Only
     those correctly configured integration instances will work. If none of the SMOMi
     integration instances are correctly configured, none of them will work.
     Users can view the OBM event details from an OBM incident record only when you
     specify the omi.mgr.id parameter correctly. If the value you specify in the corresponding
     SMOMi integration instance doesn't match the Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) which
     is automatically generated in the OBM server for the target Service Manager server and
     stored in the Incident record, users will not see the View OMi Event option from the
     Incident record.

To add and enable an Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration instance:

   1. Sign in to Service Manager as a system administrator.

   2. Click Tailoring > Integration Manager.

   3. Click Add.

     The Integration Template Selection wizard opens.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1570 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                         Service Manager 9.81

4. Select SMOMi from the Integration Template list.

               Note

             Ignore the Import Mapping checkbox, which has no effect on this integration.

5. Click Next.

6. Complete the integration instance information:

        Modify the Name and Version fields to the exact values you need.
        In the Interval Time (s) field, enter a value. For example: 600. If an OBM opened
        incident fails to be synchronized back to OBM, Service Manager will retry the failed
        task at the specified interval (for example, 600 seconds).
        In the Max Retry Times field, enter a value. For example: 10. This is the maximum
        allowed number of retries for each failed task.
        (Optional) In the SM Server field, specify a display name for the Service Manager
        server host. For example, my_Local_SM.
        (Optional) In the Endpoint Server field, specify a display name for the APM server
        host. For example, my_APM_1.
        (Optional) In the Log File Directory field, specify a directory where log files of the
        integration will be stored. This must be a directory that already exists on the Service
        Manager server host.
        (Optional) In the Log Level field, change the log level from INFO (default) to another
        level. For example, WARNING.
        (Optional) If you want this integration instance to be automatically enabled when the
        Service Manager Server service is started, select Run at system startup.
7. Click Next. The Integration Instance Parameters page opens.

8. On the General Parameters tab, complete the following fields as necessary:

1.9.1.1.10. Enable LW-SSO for the Incident
Exchange (OBM - SM) integration

Applies to User roles: System Administrator

Lightweight Single Sign-On (LW-SSO) is optional but recommended for the Incident Exchange
(OBM - SM) integration. You have different LW-SSO configuration choices depending on your
needs. The following describes how LW-SSO can be used in the Incident Exchange (OBM -
SM) integration workflow.

When OBM creates an incident from an OBM event
record

OBM creates an incident from an OBM event record by sending RESTful-based requests to
Service Manager. The incident ID is then stored in the event record.

LW-SSO is NOT needed in this process. A dedicated Service Manager user account was
specified when configuring the Service Manager integration in OBM. OBM uses this dedicated
user account when calling the Service Manager RESTful Web Service to create the incident.

When an OBM user views the incident details

The user can log in to Service Manager and view the incident details using the incident ID
stored in the event record.

If the user wants to view the incident details by clicking the incident link from the event record,
LW-SSO can be used; otherwise a Service Manager login prompt will appear.

LW-SSO is optional for this process. To enable LW-SSO for this process, configure LW-SSO in
both the Service Manager server and Web tier (because the server needs to trust the Web
tier), as well as in OBM.

When Service Manager synchronizes the OBM incident
status back to OBM

When a user has updated the OBM incident, Service Manager calls the OBM server's RESTful
Web Service to update the incident changes to the OBM event record.

LW-SSO is NOT needed in this process. A dedicated OBM user account was specified when
the Incident Exchange (OBM - SM) integration was set up in SMIS, and Service Manager uses
this user account when calling the OBM server's RESTful Web Service to synchronize the
incident status back to the OBM event record.

When a user views the event details from the OBM
incident

The user clicks the View OBM Event option from the incident to view the event details.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1580 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

LW-SSO is optional for this process. If you enable LW-SSO in the Service Manager Web tier
and in OBM, the OBM login prompt is bypassed.

1.9.1.1.11. Configure automatic closure for OBM
incidents

Applies to User Roles: System Administrator

OBM incidents can be automatically closed after a predefined amount of time since they were
last updated (or resolved if they have not been updated after being resolved).

The workflow is as follows:

   1. An incident is opened from OBM.
   2. If the Schedule Condition is met, the system creates a schedule record for the incident.

     The schedule record will expire at a future time based on the Calc Expression.
   3. A user updates the incident and saves the changes.
   4. The Reset alerts if expression on the Alerts tab of the probsummary object definition is

     evaluated. If it evaluates to true, the Expiration time of the schedule record is updated
     based on the Calc Expression. By default, the expiration time of the schedule record is
     updated only when the incident has a category of incident.
   5. When the schedule record expires, the Alert Condition is evaluated. If it evaluates to true,
     the incident is automatically closed.

To enable automatic closure for OBM incidents:

   1. Configure the global settings in the Incident Management Environment record.
        1. Click System Administration > Ongoing Maintenance > Environment Records >
           Incident Management Environment.
        2. Change the following settings as necessary.

1.9.1.1.12. Change the default assignment
group for OBM incidents

Applies to User roles: System Administrator
Service Manager can accept REST based requests from Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) to
create incidents based on events information in OBM. An incident opened from an OBM event
is automatically assigned to an existing group based on the following field values, listed from
the highest to lowest priority:

     The Affected Service of the incident
     The Category of the incident
     The Affected CI of the incident

However, if none of these field values is available, the system assigns the incident to a default
group named Application. If necessary, you can change this default group setting by
using BTO Data Model (BDM) Mapping Management as follows:

   1. Navigate to System Administration > Ongoing Maintenance > BDM Mapping
     Management. The BDM mapping configuration search page opens.

   2. Enter incident in the BDM Name field, select 1.1 in the Version field, and then click
     Search. The BDM mapping record incident opens. The Incident Exchange (OBM - SM)
     integration uses this BDM mapping record when creating an incident from an OBM event.

   3. Select the Field Mapping tab, scroll down to the assignment field in the SM Object Field
     column, and click the SM Callback field in the same row.

   4. Change Application in the following code to the name of another assignment group:

          4) A default assignment group if no other criteria is met
                        if( ! $result ) {
                                       $result = "Application";
                        }

   5. Click Save. The default assignment group is now changed.

1.9.1.1.13. Test the connection

To test the connection, send an event to the server hosting OBM that matches the filter you
defined (in the example filter, the severity value is Critical ). Next, verify that OBM forwards
the event to SM as expected.

To test the connection, do the following:

   1. On the Gateway Server system running OBM, open an Event Browser.

   2. On the system running OBM, open a command prompt and change to the following
     directory:

      <OBM_HOME>\opr\support

   3. Send an event using the following command:

      sendevent -s critical -t test111-1

   4. Verify that the event appears in the OBM Event Browser.

   5. Select the Forwarding tab.

   6. In the External Id field, you should see a valid SM incident ID.

   7. Verify that the incident appears in the Incident Management in Service Manager:

     If the event drill-down connection is correctly configured, click the hyperlink created with
     the incident ID. A browser window opens, which takes you directly to the incident in
     Service Manager.

     If you haven't configured the event drill-down connection, do the following:

        1. In the Forwarding tab in the OBM Event Browser, copy or note the incident ID from
           the External Id field.

        2. In the Service Manager user interface, navigate to Incident Management > Search
           Incidents.

        3. Paste or enter the incident ID in the Incident Id field.

        4. Click the Search button. This takes you to the incident in the Incident Details.

   8. Close the incident in Service Manager.

   9. Verify that Service Manager synchronizes the change in the state of the incident (it's now
      closed ) back to OBM. You shouldn't be able to see the closed event in SM in the active
     Event Browser, but it should now be in the History Browser.

1.9.1.1.14. Synchronize attributes

Not all attributes are synchronized back from SM to OBM by default. When the SM incident is
initially created from an OBM event, event attributes are mapped to the corresponding SM
incident attribute. Out of the box, after the initial incident creation, whenever the incident or
event subsequently changes, only a subset of the changed event and incident attributes are
synchronized. The following describes how to customize the list of attributes to synchronize
upon change.

Unidirectional synchronization: OBM to SM

OBM transfers the following attributes to SM when the event was initially created, and you have
configured the transfer of control of the event in the Connected Servers manager.

These attributes support bidirectional synchronization, but are disabled out-of-the-box.

     Title
     Severity
     Priority
     Operator: the operator assigned to the event who forwarded the event
     Category
     Subcategory
     Related CI

OBM event annotations are synchronized to SM activity log and there is no back
synchronization from SM to OBM.

Bidirectional synchronization

Attributes that support bidirectional synchronization between OBM and SM are:

     Description
     Lifecycle state (the state is only updated when the state changes to closed)
     Solution
     Contents under the Forwarding tab in the Event Details

Attribute synchronization using Groovy scripts

To change the out-of-the-box behavior regarding which attributes are updated, you can
specify this in the Groovy script used on the OBM side for synchronization or incident creation.
In the Groovy script, you can specify which fields are updated in SM, and which fields are
updated in OBM. You can also specify custom attributes in the Groovy script.

For more information, see Tips for customizing groovy scripts.

1.9.1.2. Tips for customizing groovy scripts

This section provides some tips about customizing Groovy scripts. It contains a few selected
examples of what you can customize. To see further items that can be modified, see the
configuration section of a Groovy script.
In the configuration section of the Groovy script, you can define and modify the attributes that
are to be synchronized between OBM and SM. The configuration section of the Groovy script
also contains the default value mappings for lifecycle state, severity, and priority. You can also
modify these, and it is possible to define the mappings for in-going and out-going requests
differently.
More advanced configuration can be done in other parts of the Groovy script if required.
The beginning and the end of the configuration section of the Groovy script is marked as
follows:

  //
  // configuration section to customize the Groovy script
  // BEGIN
  ...
  ...
  //
  // configuration section to customize the Groovy script
  // END

            Note

           Modifications to Groovy scripts aren't overwritten by patches and hotfixes. Your
           customized version of a script will remain after an update or a patch. If you want to
           use the newer version of a script, make a copy of your version, revert back to the
           predefined version, and then reapply your changes.

The mapping from OBM to SM is compliant to BDM 1.1 incident web service specifications. The
mapping of the BDM 1.1 incident web service to SM is specified in SM in the BDM Mapping
Manager. For more information about the BDM Mapping Manager, see the BDM Mapping
Manager section of the Service Manager online help.

Controlling attribute synchronization

You can control how updates to certain attributes are synchronized between OBM and SM by
setting some Boolean variables to true or false .
Examples:

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1592 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

      SyncAllProperties variable. By default, it is false . If you set it to true , all properties will
     be synchronized in both directions. The other variables will be ignored.

      private static final SyncTitleToSMOnUpdate = false;

     This line of the Groovy script disables the synchronization of changes to the title made in
     OBM to SM.

      private static final Boolean SyncTitleToOPROnUpdate = false;

     This line of the Groovy script disables the synchronization changes to the title made in
     SM to OBM.

The title is a required attribute in SM, and it is set, independently of the flags above, using the
title given in OBM during the creation of the incident.

Mapping OPR Lifecycle States to BDM Lifecycle States

Individual OPR event state and SM incident status changes may be selected for
synchronization. Out of the box, only the "closed" state is synchronized in both directions. To
change this behavior, add the desired states to the appropriate list, SyncOPRStatesToSM or
SyncSMStatusToOPR .

Examples:

      private static final Set SyncOPRStatesToSM = ["closed", "in_progress", "resolved"]
      private static final Set SyncSMStatusToOPR = ["closed", "resolved"]

In the example, the OPR event lifecycle states closed , in_progress , and resolved are
synchronized to the SM incident status, and SM incident statuses closed and resolved are
synchronized to the OPR event state.

            Note

           The special state "*" denotes all states, so to synchronize all OPR event states to
           the SM incident status property, specify the following:
           private static final Set SyncOPRStatesToSM = ["*"]

Additionally, two maps are used to specify the mapping of the OPR event lifecycle state to the
BDM incident status. The maps are named MapOPR2SMStatus and MapSM2OPRState . Out
of the box, all possible states have a mapping.

Examples:

      private static final Map MapOPR2SMStatus = ["open": "open", "in_progress": "work-in-
     progress", "resolved": "resolved", "closed": "closed"]

      private static final Map MapSM2OPRState = ["accepted": "open", "assigned": "open",
     "open": "open", "reopened": "open",

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1593 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

      "pending-change": "in_progress", "pending-customer": "in_progress", "pending-other":
     "in_progress",

      "pending-vendor": "in_progress", "referred": "in_progress", "suspended": "in_progress",

      "work-in-progress": "in_progress", "rejected": "resolved", "replaced-problem":
     "resolved",

      "resolved": "resolved", "cancelled": "resolved", "closed": "closed"]

Avoiding Errors with Large TQL Queries

If the Groovy script executes a TQL query that produces a large number of results, an error
message appears informing you about the TQL query result exceeding the size limit. As a
consequence, the integration event is not sent. It is possible, however, to increase this limit by
modifying the value of the tql.compound.link.max.visited.objects setting.

            Note

           To check the default value of the tql.compound.link.max.visited.objects setting,
           from the JMX console, select UCMDB:service=Settings Services, and then locate
           the showSettingsByCategory method and enter TQL Settings as the category
           name.

To modify the value of the tql.compound.link.max.visited.objects setting, follow these steps:

   1. From the JMX console, select UCMDB:service=Settings Services.
   2. Click setSettingValue.
   3. Enter tql.compound.link.max.visited.objects as the name of the setting you want to

     modify and a new value for it.

            Caution

           Increasing the value of the tql.compound.link.max.visited.objects setting also
           increases the load on the RTSM. Therefore, be sure to carefully consider how
           much to increase this value.

Syntax Errors

If you get a syntax error when customizing your Groovy scripts, you will get an event in the
event browser with a detailed description of the error. In addition, you may view the opr-
event-sync-adapter.log log file for information about how to resolve the error. You can find
this log file at the following location:

<Gateway Server root directory>/log/opr-event-sync-adapter.log

1.9.1.3. Synchronization of incident changes
back to Operations Bridge Manager (OBM)

After OBM opens an incident in Service Manager, Service Manager will synchronize the
incident changes back to OBM.

Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) can forward an event record to Service Manager as an
incident by calling a Service Manager Web Service. The incident ID is then stored in the event
record.

When a user has updated the incident opened from OBM, Service Manager calls an OBM
server RESTful Web Service to update the incident changes to the OBM event record.

If Service Manager fails to synchronize the incident changes back to OBM for some reasons
(for example, because of a network problem), Service Manager behaves as follows:

     Displays a warning message, indicating that Service Manager fails to synchronize the
     incident to OBM.
     Saves the failed task in the Service Manager Integration Suite (SMIS) task queue, and
     retries the task to synchronize the changes again to OBM based on an interval time and a
     maximum retry times configured when adding the Incident Exchange (OBM - SM)
     integration in SMIS. When the synchronization is successfully completed, the system
     removes the failed task from the task queue.

System Administrators can monitor failed tasks, and reset their retry times or rerun expired
tasks. For more information, see Monitor failover tasks.

1.9.2. Downtime exchange between OBM and
Service Manager

Operations Bridge Manager (OBM) enables you to forward downtimes (also known as
outages) from OBM to Service Manager (SM), and from SM to OBM. The downtime defined in
OBM is converted to an incident in SM, and vice versa.

Integration overview

The downtime integration between OBM and SM includes information exchanges in both of the
following directions:

     SM > OBM. When you create a downtime RfC (request for change) in SM, the RfC
     includes the CI that's under change and a start and end date/time of the downtime. If you
     don't want to waste effort with false alarms in your operations center, and don't want to
     have these times included in service availability reports, you can set up the integration so
     that these RfCs are translated to downtimes in OBM.

     In this scenario, you install a data flow probe on the CMDB:

           If you use OBM's RTSM as CMDB, install the data flow probe provided on the OBM
           installation media.

           If you use UCMDB as CMDB, install the data flow probe as described in the UCMDB
           documentation. In this case, the synchronization must also be done from UCMDB to
           OBM, additionally to synchronizing SM with UCMDB. The RfC creates a planned
           downtime CI in the CMDB, and the data flow probe DFP1 sends the planned
           downtime CI to OBM to create a downtime.

     OBM > SM. When you define downtimes using OBM , the help desk should be aware of
     such operational downtimes: After you set up the integration, downtimes in OBM trigger
     events, which create corresponding incidents in SM.

     In this scenario, when a downtime starts, OBM generates an event. Using the event
     forwarding mechanism, the event generates an incident in SM. When the downtime ends,
     an event is sent to close the downtime incident.

A single downtime can be defined on more than one CI. In the case of OBM > SM, a separate
event is sent for each CI in downtime.

     UCMDB 10.01 or higher with content pack 12 or higher.

To add the SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance, follow these steps:

   1. Click Tailoring > Integration Manager. Integration Instance Manager opens.
   2. Click Add. The Integration Template Selection wizard opens.
   3. Select SMBSM_DOWNTIME from the Integration Template list. Ignore the Import

     Mapping checkbox, which has no effect on this integration.
   4. Click Next. The Integration Instance Information page opens.

   5. Do the following:

           Modify the Name and Version fields to the exact values you need.
           In the Interval Time(s) field, enter a value based on your business needs in regard
           to downtime exchange frequency. Note that a short interval time can be safe
           because the next scheduled task will not start until the previous task is completed
           and the interval time passed.
           In the Max Retry Times field, enter a value. This is the maximum allowed number of
           retries (for example, 10) for each failed task.
           In the Log File Directory field, specify a directory where log files of the integration
           will be stored. This must be a directory that already exists on the Service Manager
           server. By default, logging message is output to sm.log .
           (Optional) In the SM Server field, specify a display name for the Service Manager
           server host. For example, my_local_SM.
           (Optional) In the Endpoint Server field, specify a display name for the APM server
           host. For example, my_APM_1.
           (Optional) In the Log Level field, change the log level from INFO (default) to another
           level. For example, WARNING.
           (Optional) If you want this integration instance to be automatically enabled when the
           Service Manager Server service is started, select Run at system startup.
   6. Click Next. The Integration Instance Parameters page opens.

   7. On the General Parameters tab, complete the following fields as necessary:

1.9.2.1.4. Tailor Service Manager to handle
phase change

Applies to User roles: System Administrator, Implementer

In the Service Manager Change Management module, authorized users can manually change
the phase of a change record. If the phase is changed to the one prior to the final approval
phase in the SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance, the system will check if there are existing planned
downtimes that have been set to Ready. If such downtimes exist, a window will open and
provide two options for the corresponding planned downtimes:

     Click Yes to withdraw the corresponding planned downtimes from UCMDB. The changes
     or tasks need to be approved again to synchronize with UCMDB at another time.
     Click No. There will be no change to the planned downtimes even if the actual status of
     the changes or tasks aren't approved.

            Note

           To disable the pop-up window when withdrawing the planned downtimes, you
           need to set the WithdrawDowntime parameter to false in the
           SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance. This operation may cause some unapproved
           planned downtimes to be synchronized to Operations Bridge Manager (OBM).

With Process Designer (PD) Content Pack 2 or later applied in Service Manager, you can tailor
the process to transit changes or tasks from one phase that's after the final approval phase in
the SMBSM_DOWNTIME instance to another that's prior to the final approval phase.To
withdraw the related planned downtime for this kind of transition, you need to add a rule set for
the transition in the Closed Loop Incident Process (CLIP) solution.

To do this, follow these steps:

   1. Go to the target workflow that needs tailoring.
   2. Select the transition that moves a phase from before the final approval phase to after the

     final approval phase.
   3. In the Rule Sets section, click Add and select the clip.downtime.withdraw rule set.
   4. Click OK to save the workflow.

1.10. Service Management Automation X
(SMAX)

Service Manager provides a Case Exchange framework to exchange data between Service
Management Automation X (SMAX) and Service Manager. The Case Exchange framework
enables you to define Service Manager as an external system with which information will be
exchanged. Hence, Service Manager has the ability to create and update records in SMAX as
well as to relate those records to records in Service Manager.

Use cases

The integration with SMAX is designed to support use cases involving a Line of Business IT
organization that's supported by a Central IT organization. It also supports use-cases involving
Central IT and other IT suppliers.

The integration enables you to exchange incidents and requests between SMAX and Service
Manager. Incident or request records created in SMAX can be assigned to a group that has
been registered to a Service Manager system. This sends the record to Service Manager for
investigation and resolution. Additional information that's added to the record, including
comments and attachments, is also exchanged with Service Manager. Updates done in Service
Manager, including activities and attachments, are sent to SMAX. It's also possible to create an
incident or request in Service Manager and exchange it with SMAX. In this case as well,
updates on either side are exchanged with the other system.

The exchanged record includes only the data necessary to create the incident or request in the
Service Manager system. The workflow phases and statuses of the record in the two systems
are independent of each other. Instead, the integration uses the concept of Operations.
Operations are additional (bi-directional) information provided on the update of a record. They
tell the receiving system what needs to be done with the record, and the system can determine
which workflow steps or data modifications need to be implemented.

Defining possible operations for the actual exchange reduces the need to perform complex
workflow mapping between the two systems. The operations are interpreted by the receiving
system and may be mapped to their existing workflow and business rules without affecting the
sending system.

Set up the integration

Implement the Case Exchange framework

For details, see General procedure.

Configure the integration

For detailed instructions, see Enable Case Exchange with SMAX.

Related topics

                                            Service Manager 9.81

1.11. Asset Manager

When ITAM and ITSM applications share common reference data related to the management
and support of IT-related Configuration Items (CIs) and these references are not available
through the CMDB, the data must be reconciled through other methods. Examples of these
references include a variety of common entities, such as employees who use CIs and the
supervisors responsible for managing them; the operating business units (that is, departments)
and physical locations where "in-service" CIs are deployed; the suppliers and service
providers of hardware and software Assets, supporting Application or Service CIs. The list
continues. A simple way to categorize this wide array of references is "People, Places and
Things."

In the case of Asset Manager (AM) and Service Manager (SM), the two repositories utilize
"synchronization type" replication to maintain the integrity of these shared common
references. Connect-It synchronizes the "People, Places and Things" between AM and SM and
provides bi-directional mapping scenarios to perform all insert and update-related transactions
in the target application. (Delete transactions must be managed within each respective
application for audit and data integrity purposes.) The following table describes related
scenarios depending on what will be synchronized and in which direction.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1621 of 1727
                                                                Service Manager 9.81

Integration direction                   Integration technology  Replicated Data
                                        Connect-It
From Asset Manager to                                                amsm-ppt.scn:

1.12. ALM Octane

ALM Octane is a web-based application lifecycle management platform that enables teams to
collaborate easily, manage the product delivery pipeline, and visualize the impact of changes.
In the integration between Service Manager (SM) and ALM Octane in your release lifecycle,
Service Manager acts as the service provider and tightly couples defect/feature
management in ALM Octane with the Change Management capabilities in SM. ALM Octane
provides REST API and enables the users to retrieve and perform CRUD (create, read, update,
delete) operations on the entities available in the Octane graphical user interface. The record
creation and update between Service Manager and ALM Octane are synchronized through
Integration Manager (SMIS) tasks in Service Manager.

This integration synchronizes SM Change to ALM Octane defect/feature for record creation.
The following scenarios are included:

     SM Change -> ALM Octane defect
     SM Change -> ALM Octane feature

After record creation, this integration implements bidirectional record updates seamlessly
between SM Change and ALM Octane defect/feature.

The overall intent of this integration is:

     Leverages SM's position as the service provider and application with the most intimate
     contact with the customer
     Efficiently tracks, reconciles, and resolves the demands placed within SM

Sample use case

The following typical use cases shed some light on how you can use this integration in your
organization.

SM Change -> ALM Octane defect

A business owner creates a Normal Change request in Service Manager and later the Normal
Change enters the Build and Test phase. On the Octane tab of the Change request, this
business owner selects the Change To Defect action, and then selects the ALM Octane
workspace. After saving these updates, the system synchronizes the Change request to a
defect in ALM Octane. Developers and QA personnel can begin working on the defect in ALM
Octane, in which the key information is synchronized from Service Manager to ALM Octane.

The integration administrator has the responsibility of determining the key information and
specifying the information in the field mapping (using the Integration Manager) in order for the
business owner to view updated (scheduled) information in Service Manager. The information
includes the Change request's title, description, severity, Octane Phase, and so on.

For complete use cases, see Synchronize Service Manager Change to ALM Octane defect.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1624 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

SM Change -> ALM Octane feature

A business owner creates a Normal Change request in Service Manager and later the Normal
Change enters the Build and Test phase. On the Octane tab of the Change request, this
business owner selects the Change To Feature action, and then selects the ALM Octane
workspace. After saving these updates, the system synchronizes the Change request to a
feature in ALM Octane. Developers and QA personnel can begin working on the feature in ALM
Octane, in which the key information is synchronized from Service Manager to ALM Octane.

Similar to the SM Change -> ALM Octane defect use case, the integration administrator has the
responsibility of determining the key information and specifying the information in the field
mapping (using the Integration Manager) in order for the business owner to view updated
(scheduled) information in Service Manager. The information includes the Change request's
title, description, severity, Octane Phase, and so on.

For complete use cases, see Synchronize Service Manager Change to ALM Octane feature.

1.12.1. Configure the settings in ALM Octane

User role: ALM Octane Administrator

See the following prerequisites that you must follow when setting up the integration between
Service Manager and ALM Octane. Ensure that you have working knowledge about ALM
Octane before you proceed.

Detailed instructions about ALM Octane administration are outside the scope of the OpenText
product suite and are hence not covered. For more information, see the ALM Octane
documentation.

Set up API access

You need to set up API access for Service Manager and grant Service Manager registered
access keys (Client ID and a Client secret) so that it can access ALM Octane. In the SM-Octane
integration, Service Manager uses the Client ID and Client secret for authentication when
synchronizing information with ALM Octane.

Follow these steps:

   1. Sign in to ALM Octane as a system administrator.
   2. Click Settings > Spaces > API ACCESS, and then click + API Access.
   3. Enter an appropriate name for the access.
   4. (Optional) Set an expiration date for the API key, and then enter a description if needed.
   5. Select the predefined roles of API and other user roles as required (for example, Team

     Member) for Service Manager to use when accessing ALM Octane.
     Select the relevant workspaces for each role. If additional relevant workspaces are
     created later, you will need to manually assign them.
   6. Click Add. A dialog displays with a Client ID and a Client secret.
     Click Copy to copy these keys to the clipboard so you can use them when configuring
     Service Manager that needs to access ALM Octane.
   7. Click OK. The access ID is added to the grid and its status is active.

Add custom fields

Octane so that the defects in ALM Octane can display the corresponding Service Manager
Change ticket ID and the name of the module table (cm3r). See the following screenshot as a
sample display of these two fields in ALM Octane:

Add the ALM Octane root CA certificate to the SM trust
store

If you are setting up an HTTPS connection, follow these steps to add the ALM Octane server
root CA certificate to the SM trust store by using the certificate generation toolkit.

   1. Export ALM Octane root CA certification to a file. For example, octaneca.crt.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1637 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

   2. Import octaneca.crt to the SM trust store. See the following sample commands.
     Non-FIPS mode:

          import-cert.bat --alias octaneca --file certs/octaneca.crt --
          keystore certs/cacerts --storepass changeit

     FIPS mode:

          import-cert.bat --alias octaneca --file certs/octaneca.crt --
          keystore certs/cacerts --storetype bcfks --storepass changeit

   3. Copy cacerts to the <SM_SERVER_HOME>/RUN folder.
   4. Update sm.ini by adding the following lines:

          truststoreFile:cacerts
          truststorePass:changeit

   5. Restart the SM server.

(Optional) Tailor the integration for more Change
categories and workflow phases

The out-of-the-box SM-Octane integration synchronizes a Normal Change request that is in
the Build and Test phase in Service Manager to an ALM Octane defect/feature. You can tailor
the integration to work with more Change category and more workflow phases so as to
increase the usability and flexibility of this integration. Regardless of the Change request's
category, all you need to do is to add the Octane tab to a target workflow phase of a Change
request.
In the SM-Octane integration, Service Manager uses the Octane tab in a Change record to
define the Octane synchronization action and Octane workspace. This tab also displays a
series of synchronization information, including Octane Id, Octane Type, Octane Phase, Octane
Last Update Time, and so on. Meanwhile, you can also select the attachments of a record on
the Octane tab so as to synchronize them to Octane. The following screenshot illustrates
the Octane tab after Service Manager synchronizes a Change record to an ALM Octane Defect.

add this tab to the corresponding form of that phase. Refer to the following steps for some
guidelines.

     when a Change enters the Validation phase, search for the chm.normal.registration
     form.

Property                                Value

This means when mapping the Severity field between a Service Manager Change and an ALM
Octane Defect, if the value of the Severity field in Service Manager is 3, the value 3 will be
mapped to medium for the Severity field in ALM Octane, and vice versa.

Get the endpoint values in ALM Octane

The following example uses Google Chrome as an example. Follow these steps to get the
endpoint values in ALM Octane:

   1. Click Settings > Spaces > LISTS, and then select a list. For example, Severity.
     ALM Octane lists contain values for list type fields. For example, the Severity list contains
     a list of possible severity values, including Low, Medium, High, Very High, and Critical.

   2. Open the Web Developer Tools in your browser, and then click the Network tab.
   3. In the Name list on the left side of the pane, select the name that begins with list_nodes?

     fields=... .
   4. Click the Preview tab on the right side of the pane, and then expand the data node to

     display all data on the list. See the following screenshot as an example:

The value for the EndPoint Values field includes both the type and id sections. For
example, {"type":"list_node","id":"list_node.severity.urgent"} .

1.12.4. Verify the integration

User role: Service Manager system administrator

SM Change -> ALM Octane defect/feature

The following example verifies the integration by synchronizing an SM Change to an ALM
Octane defect/feature.

   1. Synchronize an SM Change to an ALM Octane defect/feature.

        1. Navigate to Change Management, and then open a Normal Change record that is in
           the Build and Test phase.

        2. Click the Octane tab.

        3. To synchronize an SM Change to an ALM Octane defect, select Change To Defect in
           the Octane Action drop-down list, and then select your ALM Octane workspace in
           the Octane Workspace drop-down list.

           To synchronize an SM Change to an ALM Octane feature, select Change To Feature
           in the Octane Action drop-down list, and then select your ALM Octane workspace in
           the Octane Workspace drop-down list.

        4. Click Save and then wait for the background schedule to synchronize the Change
           record to ALM Octane. After synchronization, the Octane Id, Octane Type, Octane
           Phase, Octane Last Update Time, Synchronization Status, and Last Synchronization
           Time fields on the Octane tab have read-only values that are populated
           automatically.

           The synchronization process for attachments and new updates is unidirectional
