1.13. Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams is a chat-based workspace in Microsoft 365 that provides built-in access to
team-specific resources. The integration between Service Manager and Microsoft Teams is a
simplified collaboration model that not only enables people to exchange information in a
rapid way but also provides automated procedures to create and manage tickets.

Compared to traditional collaboration ways, the Teams integration provides the following
highlights:

     Ensure speedy resolution of critical issues by allowing IT agents to open Teams
     conversations directly from a major Incident.
     Reduce manual work, improve productivity and efficiency by automating the creation and
     management of Service Manager tickets directly in Microsoft Teams through an agent
     bot.
     Reduce IT support costs by providing knowledge article links and automating the creation
     of Service Desk tickets through a virtual agent.

Sample use cases

The following typical use cases shed some light on how you can use this integration in your
organization. Note that this isn't an exhaustive list, and the integration supports many more use
cases.

Major Incident

This use case allows the agents to collaborate on Teams with war room experience when
handling a major Incident and ensures speedy resolution of critical issues.

This integration enables an IT agent to initiate a Teams conversation from a major Incident
record and helps this agent directly contact the right people. By viewing the Incident details
(such as Incident ID, Incident Title, and Description), stakeholders including the Incident
Coordinator and Incident Manager and other IT agents can collaborate on its resolution in real-
time in the Teams channel. In the meantime, the system synchronizes all discussions to the
Incident record, which allows other Incident analysts to reuse the solutions later.

Sample screenshot:

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1649 of 1727
                                        Service Manager 9.81

For a complete use case, see Collaborate on Teams with war room experience.

Agent bot

This use case improves productivity by allowing Incident stakeholders to ask an embedded
agent bot in Microsoft Teams to open Service Manager tickets.

This integration enables an IT agent to initiate a Teams conversation with the agent bot. After
sending a command to the bot, this agent can directly open an Incident record from Teams. By
following the Incident workflows, the IT agent can update, resolve, and close this Incident - all
through a conversation with the bot in Microsoft Teams without logging on to Service
Manager. In the meantime, the system tracks all operations on the Activity tab for later
reference.

Sample screenshot:

For a complete use case, see Interact with Service Manager by using agent bot.

Virtual agent

This use case reduces IT support costs by allowing a Service Manager employee self-service
(ESS) user to view knowledge articles and then open a Service Desk ticket through an
embedded virtual agent in Microsoft Teams.

This integration enables an ESS user to initiate a Teams conversation with the virtual agent.
After describing an issue, the virtual agent responds with several knowledge articles after
performing a Smart Search in Service Manager. The ESS user can browse these knowledge
articles so as to find a solution. In case none of these articles serve as the best solution, this

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1650 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

user can ask the virtual agent to create a Service Desk ticket. Later, this user can check
the Service Desk ticket's status through the virtual agent as well.
Sample screenshot:

For a complete use case, see Interact with Service Manager by using virtual agent.

Teams notification

This use case allows Service Manager to automatically route a new notification to Microsoft
Teams as a timely reminder when an IT agent updates a record or requires further
communication. For example, when the status of an Incident becomes Resolved, the contact of
this Incident will receive a message on Teams that claims Incident IM##### has been
resolved .
Sample screenshot:

            Note

           Descriptions in this section are mainly based on Microsoft Teams version 1.5.00 at
           the time of this writing. As Teams evolves, we may not provide immediate support
           to the latest Teams features and certain functions of this integration that are related
           to these new features may be affected. We will provide continuous improvement to
           this integration to keep pace with the Teams evolvements.

1.13.1. Set up the integration for war room
experience

By setting up the integration for war room experience, IT agents can collaborate in real-time (or
anytime) in Teams channels when handling a major Incident, an Interaction, a Problem, a
Change, or a Request.
We use Microsoft Graph which exposes REST APIs and client libraries to access data on
Microsoft Teams. After an IT agent creates a conversation in a supported Service Manager
record, the system calls Microsoft Graph API through your registered Azure application to
create a message and then returns the message's web URL to the Service Manager server.
After that, the Service Manager server opens the message's web URL in Microsoft Teams and
exposes the conversation to the IT agent.
See the following illustration for Teams chat creation workflow:

The following content describes how to set up the integration between Service Manager and
Microsoft Teams. The following diagram highlights the steps.

Configure the settings on Azure

User role: Azure Administrator

See the following for prerequisites that you may need to follow when setting up the integration
between Service Manager and Microsoft Teams. Ensure that you have working knowledge
about the Microsoft 365 Developer Program and Azure Entra admin center before you proceed.

Detailed instructions about Microsoft Azure cloud services are outside the scope of the
OpenText product suite and are hence not covered. For more information, see Azure
documentation.

Register an application

Register a new Entra ID Application. Here are some guidelines for your reference when
registering an Application on Azure:

   1. Sign in to the Azure Entra admin center with an Azure account that has the Global
     administrator role.

   2. Enter a name for your Teams integration. Under Supported Account Types, select
     Accounts in this organizational directory only.

   3. Under Advanced settings, set Allow public client flows to No.
   4. Copy and save the values of the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID for later

     use.

  5. Click App Registrations > <Name of your application> > Certificates & secrets to add a
     new client secret.

     Copy and save the values of the client secret for later use.

   6. If you decide to use Authorization Code as Authorization Grant Type, you need to click
     App Registrations > <Name of your application> > Manage > Authentication and then
     add https://<SM Webtier Host>/<Context Path>/oauth/callback as the Web Redirect
     URIs. Where <SM Webtier Host>/<Context Path> should match the Web Server URL
     defined in System Information Record. For
     example: https://myserver.mydomain.com:myport/webtier/oauth/callback

  7. Click App Registrations > <Name of your application> > API permissions and then add
     the following permissions.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1654 of 1727
                                        Service Manager 9.81

                   Note

                      You must grant admin consent to the ChannelMessage.Read.All
                      permission, which synchronizes the conversation messages between
                      Teams and Service Manager. If you don’t need to synchronize
                      messages, you can skip this permission. For more information about the
                     message synchronization options in Service Manager, see Add an
                     integration instance.
                      You must grant admin consent to the ChannelMember.Read.All
                      permission, which determines the owner of the private channels. If you
                      don’t have any private channels, you can skip this permission.

Create an integration user

The Teams integration uses Authorization Code or Resource Owner Password Credentials
(ROPC) to call Graph API background, where Authorization Code allows an application to sign
in the user by token, while ROPC allows an application to sign in the user by directly handling
their password. Here are some guidelines for your reference when creating users on Azure:

   1. Sign in to the Azure Entra admin center with the Azure account you use when registering
     an application.

   2. Click Users to create a standalone Azure Entra ID user with the type of Member. This
     user is the integration user to invoke Microsoft Graph API. Alternatively, you can use the
     Azure account user directly.

   3. Add Microsoft Teams license to this user. This user isn't able to sign in to Teams without
     this license.

            Note

           If you select Resource Owner Password Credentials as Authorization Grant Type,
           you must disable security defaults on Azure and disable multifactor authentication
           (MFA) for the integration user.

           Otherwise, you need to select Authorization Code as Authorization Grant Type.

           For detailed instructions, see Security defaults in Microsoft Entra ID.

Create teams and channels in Teams

User role: Teams Integration User

This is a prerequisite for this configuration. The integration user must be the default owner of
the teams and channels that you want to use for the communication with Service Manager.

   1. For the General channel, click Manage channel. On the Channel settings tab, select Only
     owners can post messages.

   2. For the other public channels, click Manage channel. On the Channel settings tab, set
     Channel moderation to On. When you turn on moderation for a channel, only the team
     owner (the Teams integration user) can start new posts in that channel and regular users
     in the channel can only reply to existing posts and can't create new posts.

For detailed instructions, see Microsoft Teams documentation.

Configure the settings in Service Manager

User role: Service Manager System Administrator

Functionalize the Show in SM button

When a conversation starts, the system displays a Show in SM button in the default channel
messages of a record. The conversation participants can click this button and then sign in to
the Service Manager web tier to access the record on a new browser tab. See the following
screenshot as an example:

As a prerequisite, you need to enable query hash and then add web server URL to make the
Show in SM button work.

Enable query hash

Enable query hash by adding the querysecurity and queryhashcode parameters to the sm.ini
file. For example:

  querysecurity:1
  queryhashcode:<hostname.com>:13080

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1656 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

Note that you need to provide the same hostname and communication port as above for the
queryhashcode parameter in web.xml. For example:

  <param-name>serverHost</param-name>
  <param-value>hostname.com</param-value>

  <param-name>serverPort</param-name>
  <param-value>13080</param-value>

For more information, see Parameter: querysecurity and Parameter: queryhashcode.

Add the web server URL

Follow these steps:

   1. Click System Administration > Base System Configuration > Miscellaneous > System
     Information Record.

   2. Click the Active Integrations tab, and then type the web server URL in the Web Server
     URL field. For example, https://<hostname.com>:<port>/webtier/index.do
     Note that you must use the server’s Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) instead of the IP
     address in the web server URL.

   3. Click Save and OK.
   4. Restart the Service Manager server.

Synchronize the teams and channels

To synchronize the existing teams and channels to Service Manager, follow these steps:

   1. Click System Administration > Ongoing Maintenance > Collaboration > Teams Settings
     to open the Teams synchronization wizard.

   2. Select the team to synchronize, and then click OK. The Teams Team Information page
     opens.

     The system populates the Display Name, Team ID, and Description fields automatically. A
     team is active by default. If you clear the Active checkbox, all channels under the current
     team become inactive and you cannot configure the channel mappings for this team.

     In the Channels list, you can find the existing channels in the Team. Click a channel to
     open the Channel Information page on which you can view the channel information.

     If you need to synchronize another Team, click New on the Teams Team Information
     page.

            Tip

           After you add, update, or remove the teams or channels in Teams, make sure to
           wait a few minutes and then click the Synchronize button to synchronize the latest
           teams and channels information to Service Manager. If you run into an error, wait a
           few minutes as well. This is a limitation of Microsoft Graph API.

Configure Teams channel mapping

Channel mapping is an important step for connecting the conversations over the records with
the channels in Teams. To direct conversations to an appropriate Teams channel, you must
configure a series of channel mapping between Service Manager and Teams.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026                 Page 1668 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

To configure Teams channel mapping, follow these steps:

   1. Click System Administration > Ongoing Maintenance > Collaboration > Teams Settings
     to open the Teams synchronization wizard.

   2. Click Channel Mapping. Select a business module from the Module drop-down list, and
     then click Add. The Channel Mapping page opens.

                   Note

                Out-of-the-box, the Module drop-down list consists of Incident, Interaction,
                Problem, Change, and Request. To add channel mappings to another record
                type (such as Change Task), you need to manually add this module and its
                related scmessage to the Microsoft Teams Modules global list.

   3. Click Edit to build a condition or set of conditions, and then select a channel from the
     Channel list.
     See the following screenshot as an example:

  In this example, the system directs conversations over the major Incidents with the
  assignment group of E-mail / Webmail (North America) to the General channel under the
  War Room team for the MicrosoftTeams integration instance.

  Add more conditions as necessary and make sure that the conditions are reasonable. If a
  record meets multiple conditions, the system directs conversations according to the
  sequence of the mappings.

4. You can click Move Up (or press Alt+F8) or Move Down (or press Alt+F9) to arrange the
  mappings. To remove a mapping, select this mapping and then click Remove (or press
  Alt+F7).

5. Click Save and OK.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1669 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

            Note

                After you add, update, or remove the channels in Teams, make sure to
                validate the channel mappings in Service Manager.

                Make sure that the IT agents have access to the corresponding Teams
                channels especially when you update a record that affect channel mappings.
                Otherwise, the IT agents may fail to start a conversation when clicking the
                Discuss on Teams button. The error message may resemble the following:

                 We can't find that channel due to connectivity issues. Please try again later.

                If you clear the Active checkbox of a channel that already has a channel
                mapping, the corresponding channel mapping entry displays this channel as
                (Empty).

           Table, text formats, emojis, and giphys provided by Teams

           URLs

           This item is available on the Conversation tab

           Images posted by users and stickers provided by Teams

           Service Manager displays images and stickers on the Conversation tab and saves
           them to the Attachments tab with the Teams_ prefix in file names. For example,
            Teams_xxxx.png .

           User attachments that follow the type and size policy of Service Manager

           Service Manager displays the names of these attachments on the Conversation tab
           and saves these attachments to the Attachments tab.

                      more than once in the replies to the same record in Teams, Service

                      accumulating number in the file name. For example, abc (1).txt , abc

1.13.2. Set up agent bot

By embedding agent bot to Microsoft Teams, Service Manager IT agents can create Incidents
and Interactions, update, resolve, or close Incidents - all through a conversation in Microsoft
Teams without signing in to Service Manager. After an IT agent starts a Teams conversation
with the bot and sends a command, the bot calls RESTful API to query or update the record on
the Service Manager server. After that, the Service Manager server returns the query or update
result to the bot and hence the bot exposes this result to the IT agent in the Teams
conversation.
See the following illustration for the bot conversation creation workflow:

steps.

Manager and Microsoft Teams for war room experience.

User role: IT Administrator

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1678 of 1727

(sm9.80.xxxx_TeamsIntegration.zip) includes an out-of-the-box agent bot that is developed
based on Microsoft Bot Framework Composer. Extract the package to get the AgentBot folder
and then open this folder with Bot Framework Composer. You can test the bot functions first,
and then either make customization to this bot or create a new bot based on the default one.

Download and install the required software

(Optional) Customize and localize the bot

Localize the bot

The out-of-the-box bot talks to users in different languages that Service Manager supports.
However, if you need the bot to respond to a language that is unofficially supported by Service
Manager, follow these steps:

   1. Open the out-of-the-box bot with Bot Framework Composer.
   2. Update language settings and add the target language to the bot. See Multilingual support

     for detailed instructions.
   3. Localize the response strings of the bot to the target language. Open the Common file

     under Bot Responses, and then localize all response strings in #allsmmessages .

Customize the bot

You may hope to make customizations to the out-of-the-box bot by adding more actions,
updating the dialogs, and so on. For detailed instructions, see the Bot Framework Composer
documentation.

Before customizing the out-of-the-box bot, we commend backing up all response strings to
maintain consistency of the bot's behavior among the localized languages. Here are some
guidelines for your reference:

   1. Open the out-of-the-box bot with Bot Framework Composer.
   2. Open the Common file under Bot Responses, and then back up all response strings in

      #allsmmessages . You need to switch between languages to backed up the responses
     for each language.
   3. Remove all languages except for English.
   4. Make customizations to the English version of the bot by adding more actions, updating
     the dialogs, and so on.
   5. Add the supported languages back. By doing so, Composer creates a copy of your bot's
     content with the name of each additional language. Hence, your customizations maintain

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1679 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

     consistency among the languages.
   6. Switch between languages, open the Common file, and then copy the backups of the

     response strings to #allsmmessages respectively.

          // set default primary affected service to "Applications" when add
          if ($L.mode="add" and null(affected.item in $L.file)) then
          (affected.item in $L.file="CI1001030")

          // set default category when add

          $L.file=nullsub(jscall("settings.getSettingValue", "Incident",
          "default.category"), "incident"))

1.13.3. Set up virtual agent

Being embedded in Microsoft Teams, the virtual agent is a bot that is contextually aware of a
user's questions and gives relevant answers to a conversation in a natural, human-like manner.
When a Service Manager employee self-service (ESS) user starts a conversation in Teams and
describes an issue, the virtual agent leverages Smart Search and then retrieves solutions from
a variety of resources, including Service Manager Service Catalog items and Knowledge
Management (KM) documents. The ESS user can also create Interactions and check
Interactions' status by using the options provided by the virtual agent - all through a
conversation in Microsoft Teams without signing in to Service Manager.
After an ESS user starts a Teams conversation with the virtual agent, the virtual agent calls
RESTful API to send the content of the conversation to the Service Manager server. As a result,
the Service Manager server returns a valid response or knowledge search results to the virtual
agent and hence the virtual agent exposes this response or results to the ESS user in the
Teams conversation.
See the following illustration for the virtual agent conversation creation workflow:

highlights the steps.

1.13.4. Set up Teams notification

By setting up Teams notification, when an IT agent updates a record or requires further
communication, Service Manager automatically routes a new notification to Microsoft Teams
as a timely reminder. For example, when the status of an Incident becomes Resolved, the
contact of this Incident will receive a message from the integration user on Teams that claims
Incident IM##### has been resolved.

The following content describes how to set up Teams notification. The diagram below
highlights the steps.

Send Teams messages using Service Manager Rule Sets

Follow these tasks to send Teams messages using Service Manager rule sets.

Task 1: Create Teams Message templates

Service Manager provides an out-of-the-box Teams message template Incident Resolved and
the system uses this template when sending a notification through a Teams message if an
Incident's status becomes Resolved. To send Teams messages from more Service Manager
modules, you can use this template as a basis and create your own ones.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1696 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

To create a custom Teams message template, follow these steps:

   1. Click Tailoring > Notifications > Teams Message Templates.

   2. Search for and select the out-of-the-box Incident Resolved template as the base of the
     new template.

   3. On the General tab, specify a name for the new template in the Name field.

   4. Select a module from the Module drop-down list.

   5. Update the Title field if necessary.

   6. In the Content text box, design the message body of your Teams message. To reference
     a variable or expression in the message, enclose your variable or expression in braces,
     such as {$RECORD.action} .

   7. In the Subtitle text box, design the subtitle of your Teams message. To reference a
     variable or expression in the message, enclose your variable or expression in braces,
     such as {$RECORD.brief_description} .

   8. Click Add to create the new template.

A template is active by default. If you clear the Active checkbox, this Teams message template
becomes inactive and is unavailable when configuring a send Teams messages rule in Task 3.

(Optional) Task 2: Localize a template

To create a language version of a Teams message template, follow these steps:

   1. Click Tailoring > Notifications > Teams Message Templates.
   2. Use the search or advanced search to find the template that you want to localize.
   3. On the General tab, select a language in the Language field for the localized template.
   4. Keep the name in the Name field as is, because Teams message template records with

     the same name are considered language versions of one template.
   5. In the Title field, Subtitle field, and Content text box, replace the original text with the

     appropriate translation and make sure all the variables are in the correct positions.
   6. Click Add to create the localized template.

Task 3: Add a Send Teams Message rule

Service Manager provides an out-of-the-box rule set im.notification.resolved for the system
to send a Teams message to the contact of an Incident on Teams when this Incident's status
becomes Resolved. To send notifications from more Service Manager modules and from a
variety of records status, you can use the im.notification.resolved rule set as a basis and
create your own rule set.

For detailed instructions about how to add a rule for sending Teams messages, see Add a Send
Teams Message rule.

Task 4: Map your rule to a workflow

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1697 of 1727
                                                    Service Manager 9.81

The out-of-the-box rule set im.notification.resolved is mapped to Transition: Recovery -
Review in the out-of-the-box Incident workflow. After creating your rule for sending Teams
messages, use the default Incident workflow as a reference to map your rule set to the
corresponding workflows as required.

1.14. Atlassian Jira

Jira Software is a powerful work management tool for all kinds of use cases, from
requirements and test case management to agile software development. The SM-Jira
integration seamlessly incorporates Service Manager Incident/Change Management
into Jira capabilities of bug/new feature tracking and improves the efficiency of agile teams.
The overall intent of this integration is as follows.

     Automates bidirectional ticket information flow and eliminates dependency on manual
     updates between Service Manager and Jira
     Provides real-time visibility of ticket creation and status updates and ensures complete
     traceability of the tickets
     Increases collaboration across multiple Service Manager teams and Jira DevOps through
     the sharing of comments, attachments, and statuses in both applications
     Reconciles and resolves customer issues more efficiently and leverages the best
     functionalities of the delivery ecosystem

Out-of-the-box, this integration includes the following scenarios.

     Synchronize Service Manager Incident with Jira bug (SM Incident -> Jira bug)
     Synchronize Service Manager Change with Jira new feature (SM Change -> Jira new
     feature)

This section describes how to configure Service Manager and Jira for integration and how to
test the synchronization. The target readers include Consultants and Application
Administrators who must set up and maintain Jira to ensure that the synchronization meets all
user organization procedural requirements. Based on the assumption that the reader is an
experienced user of either Service Manager or Jira (but not necessarily of both), this section
describes only the basics of Service Manager and Jira.

Sample use case

The following typical use cases shed some light on how you can use this integration in your
organization.

SM Incident -> Jira bug

A business owner creates an Incident record in Service Manager. On the Jira tab of the
Incident record, this business owner selects the Incident To Bug action, and then selects the
Jira project. After saving these updates, the system synchronizes the Incident record to a bug
in Jira. Developers and QA personnel can begin working on the bug in Jira with the key
information synchronized from Service Manager.

The integration administrator has the responsibility of determining the key information and
specifying the information in the field mapping (using the Integration Manager) for the
business owner to view updated (scheduled) information in Service Manager. The information
includes but isn't limited to the Incident record's title, description, severity, and Jira Phase.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1700 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

For a complete use case, see Synchronize Service Manager Incident to Jira bug.

SM Change -> Jira new feature

A business owner creates a Normal Change request in Service Manager. On the Jira tab of the
Change request, this business owner selects the Change To New Feature action, and then
selects the Jira project. After saving these updates, the system synchronizes the Change
request to a feature in Jira. Developers and QA personnel can begin working on the feature in
Jira with the key information synchronized from Service Manager.

Similar to the SM Incident -> Jira bug use case, the integration administrator has the
responsibility of determining the key information and specifying the information in the field
mapping (using the Integration Manager) for the business owner to view updated (scheduled)
information in Service Manager. The information includes but isn't limited to the Change
request's title, description, severity, and Jira Phase.

For a complete use case, see Synchronize Service Manager Change to Jira new feature.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1701 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

1.14.1. Configure the settings in Jira

User role: Jira Project Administrator
See the following prerequisites that you must follow when setting up the integration between
Service Manager and Jira. Ensure that you have working knowledge of Jira before you
proceed.
Detailed instructions about Jira administration are outside the scope of the OpenText product
suite and are hence not covered. For more information, see the Jira documentation.

Set up API Token or Personal Access Token

In Jira Cloud, you need to set up API access for Service Manager and grant Service Manager a
registered API token so that it can access Jira;
In Jira DataCenter, you need to set up Personal Access Token for Service Manager and grant
Service Manager a registered Personal Access Token so that it can access Jira DataCetner.
In the integration, Service Manager uses the API token or Personal Access Token for
authentication when synchronizing information with Jira.
Follow these steps to set up API Token on Jira Cloud:

   1. Sign in to Jira as a project administrator.
   2. Click Your profile and settings > Manage account, and then click Security.
   3. Click Create and manage API tokens under API token, and then click Create API token.
   4. Enter an appropriate label for the token, and then click Create.
   5. Click Create. A dialog displays with a new API token.

     Click Copy to copy this token to the clipboard so you can use it when configuring Service
     Manager that needs to access Jira.
   6. Click Close. The system adds the API token to the list.

Follow these steps to set up Personal Access Token on Jira Data Center:

   1. Sign in to Jira as a project administrator.
   2. Select your profile picture at the top right corner of the screen, and then choose Profile.
   3. Once you access your profile, select Personal Access Tokens in the left-hand menu.
   4. Select Create token.
   5. Give your new token a name.
   6. Optionally, for security reasons, you can set your token to automatically expire after a set

     number of days. The EXPIRES SOON status appears 5 days before the actual expiration

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1702 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

     date. Once the token expires, you can't reactivate it. You must create a new token.

   7. Click Create.

   8. Your personal access token is created. Copy the token and store it in a safe space. Once
     you click Close you won't be able to see your Token again.

Add custom fields

You need to manually add the SM ID and the SM Table fields to Jira. Hence, the synchronized
records in Jira can display the corresponding Service Manager ticket ID and the name of the
module table (for example, cm3r ). See the following screenshot as a sample display of these
two fields in Jira:

Follow these steps to add custom fields:

   1. Sign in to Jira as a project administrator.

   2. Click Settings > Issues, and then click Custom fields under FIELDS.

   3. Click Create custom field, and the Select a Field Type window opens.

   4. Select Text Field (read only), and then click Next.
   5. Enter a name for the custom field (for example, SM ID), and then click Create.

   6. Associate the SM ID field with the appropriate screens of your project. Select the required
     screens in the list, and then click Update.

  7. Continue to follow step 2 to step 6 to add the SM Table field and associate it with the
     appropriate screens.

   8. Obtain the ID of the SM ID and SM Table fields.

     Locate the SM ID field in the Custom fields list and then click the More (⋯) icon to the
     right of this field. Select the Edit details option and then observe the URL in your browser.
     This URL contains the ID of the field. For example, https://<Jira server

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1703 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                               Service Manager 9.81

     name>.atlassian.net/secure/admin/EditCustomField!default.jspa?id=10009 . In this case,
     the ID of the SM ID field is 10009. Record this ID for later use when configuring Service
     Manager Integration Suite (SMIS) settings in Service Manager.
     Continue to follow this step and obtain the ID of the SM Table field.

(Optional) Tailor the integration for more user scenarios

The out-of-the-box SM-Jira integration synchronizes a Service Manager Incident to a Jira bug.
Meanwhile, it also synchronizes a Normal Change request that's in the Build and Test phase in
Service Manager to a Jira new feature. To increase the usability and flexibility of this
integration, you can tailor the integration to work with more user scenarios.

Scenario 1: Use Jira integration with more Change categories

Regardless of the Change request's category, all you need to do is to add the Jira tab to a
target workflow phase of a Change request.

In the SM-Jira integration, Service Manager uses the Jira tab in a Change record to define the
Jira synchronization action and Jira project. This tab also displays a series of synchronization
information, including but isn't limited to the Jira Key, Synchronization Status, and Jira Issue
Type. Meanwhile, you can also select the attachments of a record on the Jira tab so as to
synchronize them to Jira. The following screenshot illustrates the Jira tab after Service
Manager synchronizes a Change record to a Jira new feature.

To display the Jira tab in any workflow phase of a Change request, you need to manually add
this tab to the corresponding form of that phase. Next, add the corresponding rule sets to the
target workflow phase. Refer to the following steps for some guidelines.

   1. Click Tailoring > Forms Designer.

   2. Search for the corresponding form of a phase. For example, to display the Jira tab when a
     Change enters the Validation phase, search for the chm.normal.registration form.

   3. Add a Notebook Tab widget to your Change format, and then set the following property of
     the Notebook Tab widget.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1714 of 1727
                                                          Service Manager 9.81

Property                                Value
Visible Condition                       [$smJira]

4. Add a subform to the Notebook Tab widget, and then set the following property of the
  subform control.

Property                                Value
Format                                  chm.subform.jira

   5. Save your changes.

Scenario 2: Synchronize a Normal Change request to Jira
improvement

You may hope to expand the SM-Jira integration to cover more synchronization cases, such as
synchronizing a Normal Change request that's in the Build and Test phase to Jira
improvement. In this case, you need to update the Jira issue types that the Change module
supports. Refer to the following steps for some guidelines.

   1. Click Tailoring > Script Library.

   2. Search for the SMJiraCustomerConfig JavaScript.

   3. Update function supportJiraTypes(module) as follows.

      function supportJiraTypes(module) {
             if (module == "cm3r") {
                    vars.$jiraActions = ["Improvement"];
                    vars.$jiraActionsDisplay = ["Change To Improvement"];
             } else if (module == "probsummary") {
                    vars.$jiraActions = ["Bug"];
                    vars.$jiraActionsDisPlay = ["Incident To Bug"];
             }

      }

  Hence, the Change To Improvement option appears in the Jira Action drop-down list on
  the Jira tab. You can select this option manually when synchronizing a Normal Change
  request that's in the Build and Test phase to Jira improvement.

4. For the system to select Change To Improvement option automatically when
  synchronizing a Normal Change request that's in the Build and Test phase to Jira
  improvement, update function changeAutoSync(file) as follows.

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026                    Page 1715 of 1727
                                                                                                                                                Service Manager 9.81

function changeAutoSync(file) {
       var assignmentGroup = file["assign.dept"];
       var projects =

jiraUtil.getAllEnabledInstance(funcs.filename(file));
       var isEnable = isInstanceEnable(projects);
       if (isEnable && assignmentGroup == "Application") {
              vars.$jiraProject = projects[0];
              vars.$jiraAction = "Improvement";
       }

}

     Edit Options.

     Click Edit for the True option and then observe the URL in your browser. This URL
     contains a value of the option. For example, https://<Jira server
     name>.atlassian.net/secure/admin/EditCustomFieldOptions!edit.jspa?
     fieldConfigId=xxxx&atl_token=xxxx&selectedValue=10113 . In this case, the value of the
     True option is 10113. Record this value.

     Similarly, find and record the value of the False option. For example, 10114.

1.14.4. Verify the integration

User role: Service Manager system administrator

The following synchronization tasks describe how to verify the SM-Jira integration. Pay
attention to the following notes before proceeding with these tasks.

   1. Attachments and new updates synchronization

     The synchronization process for attachments and new updates is unidirectional and
     incremental. That is, you can only synchronize attachments and new updates from
     Service Manager to Jira only. Meanwhile, if you remove attachments and new updates
     from Service Manager after synchronization, the attachments and comments in Jira aren't
     affected.

   2. Formatting synchronization

     New Update

     You can enter notes in the New Update field with standard HTML formatting. However,
     when synchronizing the New Update field from Service Manager to Jira, the HTML
     formatting of the notes is lost by design and these notes appear as plain text in Jira
     comments.

     Description

     Out-of-the-box, the synchronization process for the Description field is bidirectional. It's
     notable that your input in the Description field in Service Manager is plain text, whereas
     the Description field in Jira supports formatting. By design, Service Manager doesn't
     process the formatting from Jira when synchronizing the Description field. As a result,
     descriptions with formatting from Jira may have unreadable or data loss issues after
     synchronization. Hence, keep your input in the Description field in Jira as plain text. If you
     configure other formatted fields in Jira as the Endpoint Field in field mapping, keep the
     content in such fields in plain text as well.

SM Incident -> Jira bug

The following example verifies the integration by synchronizing an SM Incident to a Jira bug.

   1. Synchronize an SM Incident to a Jira bug.

        1. Navigate to Incident Management, and then open an Incident whose status isn't
           Closed.

        2. Click the Jira tab. The background synchronization tasks start after filling in the Jira
           synchronization action and the Jira project. There are two ways: manually or
           automatically.

           To automatically fill the Jira synchronization action and the Jira project, check that
           the SMJiraCustomerConfig JavaScript exists in Script Library. The automatic

This PDF was generated on May 23, 2026  Page 1723 of 1727
                                                                                                                                         Service Manager 9.81

Incident synchronization function in this script may resemble the following.

/**

* Update the conditions for automatic synchronization of

Incident

* vars.$jiraProject: The integration instance ID

* vars.$jiraAction: The type of the Jira issue

* Example: If the assignment of the Incident is "Application",

   *                                    The current Incident record will be synchronized to

Jira's SMBT project as a Bug.

*/

function incidentAutoSync(file) {

      var assignment = file["assignment"];

      var projects =

jiraUtil.getAllEnabledInstance(funcs.filename(file));

      var isEnable = isEnstanceEable(projects);

      if (isEnable && assignment == "Application") {

          vars.$jiraProject = projects[0];

          vars.$jiraAction = "Bug";

      }

}

  You can update the parameters for isEnable && assignment , vars.$jiraProject , and
   vars.$jiraAction as required to redefine the conditions for automatic Incident
  synchronization.

  Otherwise, manually select Incident To Bug in the Jira Action drop-down list, and
  select the Jira project (project alias) in the Jira Project drop-down list. Save this
  Incident to commence the synchronization process.

3. After Service Manager runs the integration background process, Jira creates a bug.
  In Service Manager, the Jira Key, Jira Phase, Synchronization Status, Jira Issue
  Type, and Last Synchronization Time fields on the Jira tab have read-only values
  that are populated automatically.

Jira Phase                              The bug's status in Jira.
Synchronization Status                  The synchronization status.
Jira Issue Type                         Bug.
Last Synchronization Time               The last synchronization time between
                                        SM and Jira.

   2. Update some fields, add attachments, and then perform synchronization again from the
     SM Incident to the Jira bug.

        1. Open the Incident record again and then update the title, description, and urgency
           information.

        2. Click the Activities tab. Select Update to external service in the Update Type drop-
           down list, and then enter some notes in the Update field.

        3. Click the Attachments tab and add some attachments to the Incident record. Save
           your updates.

        4. Click the Jira tab and then click Add to select the attachments from the current
           Incident record for Jira synchronization.

        5. Click Save and then wait for the next synchronization.

   3. View the synchronization result in the Jira bug.

     Click View in Jira. Sign in to Jira and open the bug record. Check that your updates to the
     title, description, and urgency in the SM Incident record are synchronized to the
     corresponding fields in the Jira bug record. Meanwhile, your notes in the SM Update field
     now appear as comments in the Jira bug record. Your selected attachments in the SM
     Incident record now appear as the Jira bug record's attachments as well.

For a complete use case, see Synchronize Service Manager Incident to Jira bug.

The following example verifies the integration by synchronizing an SM Change to a Jira new
feature.

   1. Synchronize an SM Change to a Jira new feature.

        1. Open the workflow of a Normal Change and click the Build And Test phase. Make
           sure that the chm.jira.enter rule set exists in On enter and the
           chm.jira.assignproject rule set exists in On update.

2. Navigate to Change Management, and then open a Normal Change record that's in
  the Build and Test phase.

3. Click the Jira tab. The background synchronization tasks start after filling in the Jira
  synchronization action and the Jira project. There are two ways: manually or
  automatically.

  To automatically fill the Jira synchronization action and the Jira project, check that

/**

* Update the conditions for automatic synchronization of Change

* vars.$jiraProject: The integration instance ID

* vars.$jiraAction: The type of the Jira issue

* Example: If the assignmentGroup of the Change is

"Application",

   *                                    The current Change record will be synchronized to

Jira's SC project as a New Feature

*/

function changeAutoSync(file) {

      var assignmentGroup = file["assign.dept"];

      var projects =

jiraUtil.getAllEnabledInstance(funcs.filename(file));

      var isEnable = isEnstanceEable(projects);

      if (isEnable && assignmentGroup == "Application") {

         vars.$jiraProject = projects[0];

         vars.$jiraAction = "New Feature";

      }

}

  You can update the parameters for isEnable && assignment , vars.$jiraProject , and
   vars.$jiraAction as required to redefine the conditions for automatic Change
  synchronization.

  Otherwise, manually select Change To New Feature in the Jira Action drop-down
  list, and select the Jira project (project alias) in the Jira Project drop-down list. Save
  this Change to commence the synchronization process.
